moments.selftext: BREAKING: The US Government officially posts its largest July budget deficit in history, at -$432 billion, due to an acceleration in federal spending. Interest on US debt rose +$26 billion from last July's levels to an alarming $118 billion for the month. This puts total interest expense for FY2026 up to $1.17 trillion in FY2026. As a result, interest expense has officially surpassed both National Defense and Medicare spending. In other words, the US government now spends more money just on interest than it does to fund the entire US Military or to provide healthcare for seniors. We cannot afford higher interest rates.

moments.title: In 2015, a Virginia jury awarded $500,000 to a patient whose phone accidentally recorded his medical team while he was under sedation. He had intended to record his doctor’s post-procedure instructions, but the recording
moments.selftext: In 2015, a Virginia jury awarded $500,000 to a patient whose phone accidentally recorded his medical team while he was under sedation. He had intended to record his doctor’s post-procedure instructions, but the recording captured anesthesiologist Tiffany Ingham and gastroenterologist Soloman Shah making disparaging remarks about him. The audio reportedly included insults about his intelligence, a false claim that he had syphilis, and comments about avoiding him after the procedure. The case ultimately resulted in an award for defamation, medical malpractice, and punitive damages.

moments.title: Waitress Melina Salazar spent nearly seven years serving a notoriously rude customer who never left her a tip. When he died, she discovered that despite his behavior, he had named her in his will and left her $50,000. Fo
moments.selftext: Waitress Melina Salazar spent nearly seven years serving a notoriously rude customer who never left her a tip. When he died, she discovered that despite his behavior, he had named her in his will and left her $50,000. For nearly seven years, waitress Melina Salazar was the only server at a Luby’s Cafeteria in Brownsville, Texas, willing to regularly serve Walter “Buck” Swords. The 89-year-old World War II veteran had a reputation for being difficult, often cursing at staff, complaining about his meals, and insisting that his food be served extremely hot. He never left a tip. When Swords died in 2007, Salazar received an unexpected surprise. His estate lawyer informed her that Swords had left her $50,000 in cash and his 2000 Buick in his will, reportedly as a thank-you for the patience and kindness she had shown him over the years.
